articles.title: Canvas Breach Disrupts Schools & Colleges Nationwide
articles.summary: AI is now hunting vulns faster than humans can patch them, and May's Patch Tuesday is basically a greatest hits album of machine-discovered security disasters. When the robots start finding our bugs better than we do, maybe it's time to panic just a little.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft dropped 167 security fixes including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Meanwhile Chrome patched its fourth zero-day this year because apparently browser security is just a suggestion now.

articles.title: NGINX CVE-2026-42945 Exploited in the Wild, Causing Worker Crashes and Possible RCE
articles.summary: MiniPlasma zero-day grants SYSTEM privileges on fully patched Windows boxes because why should security updates actually secure anything? Courtesy of the legend Chaotic Eclipse, who keeps making Microsoft's patch cycle look like performance art.

articles.title: Grafana GitHub Token Breach Led to Codebase Download and Extortion Attempt
articles.summary: CVE-2026-42945 in NGINX is being exploited in the wild just days after disclosure, causing worker crashes and potential RCE. Because apparently giving attackers a roadmap to your infrastructure is the new responsible disclosure.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned hard, disrupting schools nationwide while hackers defaced login pages with ransom demands threatening to leak student data. Nothing says 'modern education' like your homework being held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: MPs want social media treated more like unsafe toys than harmless apps
articles.summary: OpenAI got caught in a supply chain attack when malware-laced npm packages compromised employee devices and stole internal credentials. Even the AI overlords aren't immune to good old-fashioned social engineering through package managers.

articles.title: Funnel Builder Flaw Under Active Exploitation Enables WooCommerce Checkout Skimming
articles.summary: Grafana's GitHub got compromised, letting attackers download their entire codebase and attempt extortion. At least they're claiming no customer data was touched, which is corporate speak for 'we have no idea what else they grabbed.'

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram killed its end-to-end encryption feature instead of making it default, breaking years of privacy promises. Meta chose surveillance capitalism over user security, shocking absolutely no one who's been paying attention.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Microsoft Exchange Server to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Pwn2Own Berlin 2026 delivered 47 zero-days and $1.3M in payouts, with DEVCORE absolutely dominating every category. This is how you properly incentivize bug hunting instead of letting vulns fester in corporate denial.

articles.title: MiniPlasma Windows 0-Day Enables SYSTEM Privilege Escalation on Fully Patched Systems
articles.summary: Analysis reveals Fast16 malware was sabotaging nuclear weapons simulations before Stuxnet even existed, corrupting uranium-compression calculations. Turns out cyberwar against nuclear programs has deeper roots than anyone suspected.
